add.issue.name: Hypr: stop new windows auto-joining a window group

edit.description.md:
Hyprland's group:auto_group defaults to true, so a window opened while a grouped window has focus joins that group and takes over the workspace as a group tab instead of tiling. Opening a terminal looked like it went fullscreen over everything, and SUPER+G (group toggle) was the only way out. Pressing that key on an ungrouped window creates a group of one, which arms the same trap for the next window, so the fix kept recreating the problem.

Set auto_group = false and drag_into_group = 0 in the group block of Configs/hypr/hyprland.lua. New windows tile; grouping by hand on SUPER+G still works.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: the group block in Configs/hypr/hyprland.lua now sets auto_group = false and drag_into_group = 0, so a new window tiles instead of joining the focused window's group and filling the workspace as a tab.

PR: https://github.com/T-Crypt/aphotic-hypr/pull/312

Verified with Hyprland --verify-config (config ok, and an invented key in the same file is reported as unknown, so the check is real), a live repro with throwaway windows both with the setting on and off, and tools/ci/local.sh --here (bash-syntax pass, 78 bash test files pass, pytest 279 passed 2 skipped). No VM run needed: no installer, profile or systemd unit is touched.

add.issue.name: skills plugin: a workspace plane over skills-manager-cli

edit.description.md:
Add a `skills` plugin to aphotic-plugins: a workspace plane, a Settings pane and an `aphotic skills` command over the upstream `skills-manager-cli`, so one shared agent-skill library serves Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and the rest.

## Why
Upstream (xingkongliang/skills-manager) already owns the hard parts: central library, source metadata, per-agent deployments, presets, tags, update tracking and skill-aware git merging. Reimplementing that is months of work and a second copy of an MIT project. The plugin is a front end, the same way llama-swap wraps a model server and llm-fit wraps llmfit.

## Scope
- One plugin, several surfaces: `[ui.workspace]`, `[ui.settings_pane]` under AI, an `[action]`, a `[keybind]`, and `[cli] command = "skills"`.
- Reads: library list, tag and source filters, per-agent deploy state, SKILL.md preview.
- Writes: deploy and undeploy a skill for one agent or many, preset apply, tags, adopt.
- One CLI resolution rule shared by the shell command and the QML service, so the UI can never pick a different binary than the CLI does.
- Library path stays the CLI default, so the desktop app and Aphotic read the same library instead of two divergent copies.

## Not in v1
Project workspaces, linked workspaces, the backup and conflict UI, tray, in-app updates, translations. Follow-up on this ticket.

## Supply chain
Pin v1.42.0 and record the Linux x64 asset sha256 in the plugin. Upstream publishes signatures for the installers but not for the CLI asset, so this is trust on first use, re-verified on every later run. A mismatch fails closed.

## Verification
- tests/test_contract.sh: pinned version, JSON shapes for list and status, and one TARGET_CONFLICT error path.
- tests/test_install_deps.sh: headless run installs nothing, a hash mismatch fails.
- Windowless `qs` probe for the service, never `qs -p .` on a live desktop.
- python3 tools/build_index.py --check and aphotic plugin validate skills.

add.issue.name: ios-dev plugin: iOS toolchain doctor, run and debug from the shell

edit.description.md:
One plugin, gated on the `dev` layer, that turns a Linux machine into an iPhone development box and drives it from the shell's own surfaces.

Scope of this ticket:
- `ios-dev/` in the plugin repo, with `requires_layer = "dev"` on every surface, action and keybind, so the plugin is offered only to machines carrying the `dev` layer.
- `aphotic ios` as the plugin's own top-level command: doctor, setup, new, run, debug, stop, devices, toolchain, status.
- Three surfaces: the Workspace plane, a collapsed Settings section, and a notch tile labelled iOS.
- Three actions and one keybind, `SUPER + ALT + I`, bound through compositor IPC rather than written into a config file.
- The toolchain doctor reports which prerequisites are missing and prints the one instruction no script can carry out, which is downloading the matching Xcode archive from Apple in a browser.

Out of scope here, each gets its own ticket: hot reload, shipping an ipa to TestFlight, and a profile registration so a build claims resources through the engine.

No core change is needed. Every surface this uses is already hosted, and `dev` is already in the gate vocabulary.

add.issue.comment.md:
PR: https://github.com/T-Crypt/aphotic-plugins/pull/49

First phase landed on `feature/ios-dev`, cut from `origin/main` at 2c556eb. Four commits: the engine and CLI, the three QML surfaces, the catalogue row, and a text pass.

Verified here: `ios-dev/tests/test_ios_dev.sh` passes, `aphotic plugin validate` returns ok with four warnings (the two declared binaries absent from this machine), `tools/build_index.py --check` passes, and a windowless `qs` probe compiled and instantiated all five QML files with clean exit 0.

Not verified here, because this machine has no Swift toolchain, no Darwin SDK, no xtool and no iPhone: `aphotic ios setup` end to end, `aphotic ios new` producing a project, `aphotic ios run` reaching `xtool dev run`, and the full `aphotic plugin install ios-dev --link` lifecycle, which was skipped because it would have pulled `usbmuxd` and `inotify-tools` through the AUR helper. The probe also found three real defects, all fixed: two components missing the import that provides Colours, the run action missing the one that provides DevProfile, and a partial default state literal that threw a TypeError on a machine that had never run setup.

Remaining phases, one ticket each: hot reload, the debugger attach, log streaming, shipping to TestFlight, and the profile registration.

add.issue.name: Install: Flatpak apps as a profile extension point

edit.description.md:
Flatpak has no home in the profiles. Add an optional `[flatpak] apps = [...]` table to base and layer TOMLs plus a `custom_flatpaks.lst` drop-in mirroring `custom_apps.lst`, so a profile can install Flatpak apps the same declarative way it installs packages.

Scope: merge.py gains a `flatpak` field and `--custom-flatpaks`; new lib/install/flatpak.sh (ensure Flathub, idempotent install via `flatpak info --system`, optional-skip on failure) wired into install.sh stage 5 with a dry-run section; uninstall.sh --purge-packages removes the profile's Flatpak apps; package checkers validate Flatpak IDs against Flathub and never feed them to pacman -Si; tests updated (merge, repo layout, dry-run, shell-deps) plus the `[flatpak]` theme extension tied to the Settings gtkTheme default.

VS Code stays a pacman package on purpose: the Super+C keybind runs a bare `code`, which a Flatpak does not put on PATH, and ticket XQ9Q88Y already plans a signed pacman build with no AUR compile.
